BiblicalUsage: Lael appears once, as the father of a chief of the Levites in Numbers 3:24. His son Eliasaph was set over the Gershonites in the wilderness, and his name means of God.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Lael's one verse is enough: a father whose son was set over the service of the tabernacle, and a name that says he belonged to God.
